title: Use Multiplication to Determine Area
goal: I can find the area of a rectangle by multiplying its length and width.
catchAll: Area of a rectangle = length × width. Then name the unit: square units, square feet …

teacher.def: to find the area of a rectangle, you multiply the length and the width
number of unit squares needed to cover the INSIDE of a shape or region

glossary.length: how long the rectangle is (the side along the top)
glossary.width: how wide the rectangle is (the side along the left)
glossary.multiply: find the total of equal rows: 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20

screens.title: Rows are equal groups
text: A rectangle covered by squares has equal rows.
4 rows of 5 squares is 4 × 5. Multiplying is a quick way to count them all: 20.
screens.caption: 4 rows of 5: 4 × 5 = 20

screens.title: Length × width
text: The length tells how many squares fit in a row. The width tells how many rows there are.
So area = length × width. You can multiply without drawing every square.
screens.caption: 7 cm × 3 cm = 21 square centimeters

item.prompt: A rectangle is 6 units long and 2 units wide. What is its area in square units?
hints: Multiply the length and the width.

screens.title: Squares are rectangles too
text: A square has the same length and width.
A square 5 cm on each side: 5 × 5 = 25 square centimeters.

screens.title: Say the unit
text: Sides in centimeters give square centimeters. Sides in inches, feet, yards or meters give square inches, square feet, square yards or square meters.
Always write the area with a square unit.

screens.title: From an area to its sides
text: Sometimes you know the area and look for the sides.
Find two numbers that multiply to the area. An area of 12 square feet could be 3 feet by 4 feet, or 2 feet by 6 feet.
screens.caption: 3 × 4 = 12, so 3 ft by 4 ft works

item.prompt: Which equation finds the area of a rectangle 9 feet long and 4 feet wide?

options.why: Adding the sides does not find area.
That adds all the sides around the outside. Area covers the inside.

watch.takeaway: Area of a rectangle = length × width. Multiplying gives the same answer as counting every square, faster.

steps.say: Problem: what is the area of the rectangle?
Step 3: Write the equation: area = length × width.
Step 4: Name the unit: 21 square centimeters.
Step 5: Check with the picture: 3 rows of 7 squares.

why.prompt: Why does 7 × 3 give the same answer as counting?

options.text: There are 3 equal rows of 7 squares.

options.why: Odd numbers do not matter. Equal rows do.

options.text: It does not; counting is different.

examples.title: Example B: a grid with no numbers

steps.say: Problem: the side lengths are not written. What is the area?
Step 1: Count the squares in one row: 6. That is the length.
Step 2: Count the rows: 4. That is the width.
Step 4: The area is 24 square units.
Problem: a square window is 5 feet on each side. What is its area?
Step 1: A square has the same length and width: 5 and 5.
Step 3: The window covers 25 square feet.

sections.heading: What your child is learning
sections.text: Your child finds the area of a rectangle by multiplying length × width (the teacher's words: "to find the area of a rectangle, you multiply the length and the width"), and labels it in square units.

sections.heading: Try it with real things
list: Measure a book or a placemat with a ruler and multiply the sides.
Draw a rectangle on graph paper, count the squares, then check by multiplying.

sections.heading: Questions to ask
list: Which side is the length? Which is the width?
What unit are the sides in? So what unit is the area?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Adding the sides (7 + 3) instead of multiplying (7 × 3).
Writing "21 cm" instead of "21 square centimeters".
Adding all four sides (that measures around the outside).
